questions.question: A parent renders <Badge label="New" />. How should Badge receive the label?

options.b: By looking for a DOM element named label
options.c: By creating an effect with no dependencies
options.d: By reading the parent's state object directly

questions.explanation: The parent passes label as a prop. Badge reads it from its props parameter.

questions.question: Which key should be used for rows that can be reordered and have a stable unique database ID?

options.b: A random value generated on every render
options.d: The number of rows in the list

questions.explanation: A stable key lets React match a row to the same component identity across reorders.

questions.question: Starting with count = 0, one click handler calls setCount(count + 1) twice. What is count after React processes those updates?
questions.explanation: Both calls read the handler's snapshot of count and request replacement with 1.

questions.question: Which handler reliably adds two to the latest pending count with two state updates?
questions.explanation: Each updater receives the state produced by the preceding queued update.

questions.question: Which operations are appropriate inside the render of a React component? Select all that apply.

options.a: Calculate a filtered list from props
options.b: Send an analytics event for each render
options.c: Mutate a shared object imported from another module

questions.explanation: Pure calculations and JSX belong in render. Sending events and mutating external state are side effects.

questions.question: An input must display React state and update that state when a user types. Which pair makes it a controlled text input?
questions.explanation: The value prop controls what is displayed, and onChange updates the state backing that prop.

questions.question: Sibling components need to display and edit the same selected tab. Where should that shared state usually live?

options.b: A separate useState in each sibling
options.c: A random sibling selected on each render

questions.explanation: Lifting state to a common parent gives both siblings one shared source of truth through props.

questions.question: A useEffect connects to a chat room and returns a disconnect function. What happens when roomId changes and roomId is a dependency?

options.a: Only the old connection is closed
options.b: The old effect cleans up before the new effect sets up
options.c: Both connections remain until the page unloads
options.d: The effect never runs after the first render

questions.explanation: When a dependency changes, React runs cleanup for the previous effect before running the replacement setup.

questions.question: A button should submit an order only when clicked. Where should the submission call normally go?

options.c: In an effect that runs on mount

questions.explanation: The submission is a consequence of the user's click, so the event handler is the direct trigger.

questions.question: Which actions fit the normal rules for built-in Hooks such as useState and useEffect? Select all that apply.

options.a: Call useState inside an event handler
options.b: Call useState unconditionally at the top level of a component
options.c: Call useEffect at the top level of a custom Hook
options.d: Call useEffect inside an array map callback

questions.explanation: These Hooks are called at the top level of components or custom Hooks so their call order is consistent.

questions.question: A component needs to remember a timeout ID between renders. Changing the ID does not need to update the UI. Which Hook fits?
questions.explanation: A ref persists across renders. Changing its current value does not request a render.

questions.question: A component displays a total that can be calculated from its current items prop. What is the simplest way to avoid storing stale totals?

options.a: Initialize local total state once from items
options.b: Copy each total into a mutable global object
options.c: Compute the total from items during render
options.d: Update the total only when the component unmounts

questions.explanation: Calculating the total from current props avoids a second value that could fall out of sync.

questions.question: A profile editor should reset its local form state when it switches from one user to another. Which parent change directly gives each user a different component identity?

options.a: Change a className on the same editor
options.b: Pass a different key based on user ID
options.d: Pass a fresh object as a prop on each render

questions.explanation: A different key makes React replace the previous instance and initialize fresh local state.

questions.question: A child uses useContext(ThemeContext). Which value does it read when the same context has two nested providers above it?

options.a: The default value passed to createContext

questions.explanation: React looks upward from the consumer and uses the nearest matching provider.

questions.question: Which updates preserve React state immutability for a list of objects? Select all that apply.

options.a: Replace one row with a new object using map
options.b: Call push directly on the existing state array
options.d: Build a new array with the spread operator when appending a row

questions.explanation: map and spread can construct new arrays. The changed row should also be represented by a new object.

questions.question: What does useReducer return to the calling component?

options.a: The current state and a dispatch function
options.b: The current state and a function to replace the reducer
options.c: The reducer's source code and its dependency list
options.d: A mutable ref and an effect cleanup function

questions.explanation: Dispatch sends actions to the reducer, which computes the next state.

questions.question: Which value can a React component return when it should render no visible output?

options.a: A plain object with an empty props field
options.b: A DOM node created by document.createElement

questions.explanation: Returning null tells React to render nothing for that component.

questions.question: What is useMemo intended to cache between renders while its dependencies stay unchanged?

options.c: A server response automatically across all users

questions.explanation: useMemo caches a calculation result as a performance optimization.

questions.question: An effect starts a window event listener. What should its cleanup do?

options.c: Clear all event listeners on the page
options.d: Remove the listener that this effect registered

questions.explanation: Cleanup reverses the setup so old listeners do not accumulate across updates or after unmounting.

questions.question: Which values are good candidates to derive during render from existing state? Select all that apply.

options.a: A cart total computed from cart items
options.b: The text a user has typed but has not yet submitted
options.c: The count of items matching a stored search query

questions.explanation: The total and filtered count are calculations from existing inputs. The input text and sort choice can change independently.
